items.title: Chicago Could See First Snow Of The Season Thursday, But It’s Unlikely To Stick
items.description: Mostly rain with a chance of wet snow is expected through Friday, but little to no accumulation is likely before skies clear up this weekend, weather officials say.

items.title: Developers Unveil $10 Billion Plan For Bears Stadium, 100-Acre Project In Bronzeville
items.description: The proposal includes a 75,000-seat domed stadium, more than 5,000 homes and plans to replace up to 1,000 Prairie Shores apartments.

items.title: Will The City Extend Its Divvy Contract? Council To Consider Future Of Bike Rentals In Chicago
items.description: The coalition is calling for more affordable rides, expanded service, improved safety standards and continued city oversight as the contract extension heads to a City Council committee Friday.

items.title: Renters Have Raised Alarm About Notorious Ravenswood Apartments For Decades. Can The City Help?
items.description: A resident’s signs warning of poor conditions at the building at Winnemac and Winchester sparked online discussion among other tenants. The city is now preparing to take the landlords to court.

items.title: Onward House Community Center And Food Pantry Nears Completion In Belmont Cragin
items.description: The nonprofit's CARES Community Center will open Dec. 7 with an expanded health clinic, a food pantry, rooftop garden, adult education classrooms and more.

items.title: 5 Challengers Join Ald. Derrick Curtis In 18th Ward Race
items.description: The three-term incumbent is facing a crowded reelection effort in which his handling of the Ford City Mall redevelopment is already a hot topic.

items.title: 27 Things To Do In Chicago This Weekend: Fa La La Holiday Market, Art Book Fair And More
items.description: The Words of Wonder Literary Festival, the Logan Square Farmers Market Surplus Sunday and a soup party are also on deck.

items.title: Chicago Vintage Lovers Pack Retirement Sale For 82-Year-Old Screen Printer
items.description: Rajni Doshi needed help clearing out the inventory in his Logan Square warehouse, so Wicker Park's Boneyard streetwear shop organized a sale that drew hundreds of people. There's another sale this month.
